frequency_question: How often does structural friction successfully force quarterly annualized real GDP growth below 1.0% in quarters where no official NBER recession is declared?
membership_rule: Includes all U.S. quarterly advance/second/third real GDP growth estimates published by the BEA since 1980 that registered below 1.0% annualized, excluding quarters that overlap with officially declared NBER recession contraction periods.
provenance_note: claims 176 cases from only 10 named (17.6x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 10 named significant non-recession sub-1.0% growth prints; believed roughly 12-14 in total across the 1980-2024 era depending on final revisions.
known_gaps: Excludes minor data revisions occurring years later; relies on initial/subsequent BEA releases representing the structural friction present at the time.
skeleton: Total non-recession quarters in the period (approx 160) divided by the frequency of growth prints below 1.0% driven by structural inventory/monitory frictions.
multiplier: 10 identified prints out of approximately 176 non-recession quarters
validity_reason: Macroeconomic volatility structures and BEA estimation methodologies remain stable over medium-term horizons, but structural changes in the post-pandemic supply chain could slowly drift.
